answer: A headland night watch screens new keys. The applicant stakes 19.7 POA and hangs a 7-byte transponder behind one licensed umber canvas aimed at beacon BH-12. For six hours they flash a 4-byte reply every 8 minutes, only while the tide staff stands between 2.6 and 3.1 meters. Two shore clerks recompute the panel ID from the epoch seed and permit one transponder per canvas. Raising 2,800 aliases needs 2,800 unshared panels and 126,000 in-band flashes. A second hang on the same canvas, a missed flash, or an out-of-band tide reading burns 67% of the stake and darkens that panel for twelve epochs.
